bull.b: Strong, accelerating ARR reflects durable subscription momentum and multi-module adoption of the Falcon platform. High net new ARR and expanding ending ARR signal sticky customer relationships and predictable recurring revenue that underpin sustainable top-line growth and long-term cash conversion.

Consistent, expanding free cash flow provides durable financial flexibility to fund R&D, M&A, and share buybacks while insulating the business from earnings volatility. Strong cash conversion supports reinvestment in product and go-to-market, strengthening long-term competitive positioning.

Sustained high subscription gross margins reflect a scalable cloud-native delivery model and operating leverage. Margin expansion driven by cloud optimization improves long-term profitability potential and funds margin-accretive investments in AI detection and platform expansion.

bear.b: Persistent divergence between GAAP and non‑GAAP metrics means reported earnings remain volatile and can obscure true economic returns. Over time this gap can limit traditional profitability measures, complicate comparability, and pressure investor confidence if GAAP profits are inconsistent.

Material upside is tied to continued enterprise AI adoption. If AI rollout slows or security adoption lags, expected platform monetization and module expansion may underperform. This structural dependency raises execution risk over the medium term for revenue and ARR trajectories.

A growing equity base with negative ROE indicates the company has yet to consistently convert capital into GAAP profits. Over months this can pressure return-based metrics and signal that scale benefits haven't fully translated to accounting profitability, affecting long-term shareholder returns.
